sentences: Piet Mondrian painted this small canvas, just 45 centimetres square, in Paris in 1930.
Black vertical and horizontal lines divide the surface, and only the three primaries, red, blue and yellow, sit among the white.
The large red square at the upper right shares its weight with a small blue at the lower left and an even smaller yellow at the lower right.
There is no symmetry anywhere, yet nothing wobbles, because the size of each area and the weight of each colour are tuned so precisely.
Mondrian stripped away every trace of nature to show a universal harmony with line and primary colour alone, an approach he called Neo-Plasticism.
The painting was made at the request of the Zurich architect Alfred Roth, and on the back Mondrian wrote a dedication about seeking relationships and balance as a way of preparing the future.
Roth gave it to the Kunsthaus Zürich in 1987.
